chunks.label: Mum and dad
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk to and about your parents and other people's.
chunks.interference: haha and chichi are your own parents to outsiders; okaasan and otousan are others' parents, or yours to their face.

chunks.label: Family and parents
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your family and parents as a group.
chunks.interference: ryoushin is your own parents; goryoushin is someone else's.

chunks.label: Older brother and sister
chunks.rationale: Lets you mention your older siblings and ask about someone else's.
chunks.interference: ani and ane are your own; oniisan and oneesan are others', or yours to their face.

chunks.label: Siblings and younger ones
chunks.rationale: Lets you say how many siblings you have and which ones.
chunks.interference: otouto (younger brother) starts like otousan (father).

chunks.label: Husband and wife
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your spouse and ask about someone else's.
chunks.interference: tsuma and otto are your own spouse; okusan and goshujin are someone else's.

chunks.label: Sons and daughters
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about your children and ask about other people's.
chunks.interference: Plain musuko and musume are your own; add -san for someone else's.

chunks.label: Grandparents
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk to and about grandparents and elderly people.
chunks.interference: ojiisan and obaasan (grandparents) differ from ojisan and obasan (uncle, aunt) only by the long vowel.

chunks.label: Mum and dad at home
chunks.rationale: Lets you call your parents the way families do at home.
chunks.interference: With outsiders adults switch to chichi and haha.

chunks.label: Calling siblings at home
chunks.rationale: Lets you call your older siblings the way families do.
chunks.interference: niichan and neechan also hail strangers and can sound rough.

chunks.label: Uncles, aunts and relatives
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about the wider family.
chunks.interference: ojisan and obasan also mean any middle-aged man or woman; mind the short vowel.

chunks.label: Married couple words
chunks.rationale: Lets you understand the casual and older words couples use.
chunks.interference: shujin and danna are your own husband; goshujin and dannasan are someone else's.

chunks.label: Family roles
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe parents and eldest children as roles.
chunks.interference: chichioya and hahaoya describe a role; they are not what you call your parents.

chunks.label: Grandparents and grandchildren
chunks.rationale: Lets you mention your grandparents and grandkids politely.
chunks.interference: sofu and sobo are your own grandparents in polite talk; at home say ojiichan and obaachan.

chunks.label: Rough home words
chunks.rationale: Lets you understand the homely or blunt words people use for family.
chunks.interference: oyaji and ofukuro are men's words for their own parents; oyaji also means any middle-aged man.

chunks.label: Face
chunks.rationale: Lets you name the parts of your face.
chunks.interference: hana (nose) sounds like hana (flower); me is one short sound and easy to miss.

chunks.label: Head and shoulders
chunks.rationale: Lets you say where it hurts above the chest.
chunks.interference: kami (hair) sounds like kami (paper, god).

chunks.label: Hands and feet
chunks.rationale: Lets you name your limbs and fingers.
chunks.interference: ashi covers both leg and foot; te often covers the arm too.

chunks.label: Belly, back and chest
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about hunger and aches in the body.
chunks.interference: onaka is the everyday word; hara is blunt and mostly male.

chunks.label: Teeth, throat and lips
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe toothache, sore throats and dry lips.
chunks.interference: shita (tongue) sounds like shita (below); ha (tooth) like ha (leaf).

chunks.label: Lower back and legs
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe back pain and leg injuries.
chunks.interference: koshi is the lower back, not the whole back (senaka).

chunks.label: Hair, skin and nails
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about grooming and how skin looks.
chunks.interference: kami no ke and kami are the same hair; ke alone is body hair.

chunks.label: Left, right, both
chunks.rationale: Lets you say which hand, or the whole body.
chunks.interference: None.

chunks.label: I and you
chunks.rationale: Lets you say I and you in casual talk.
chunks.interference: ore is men-only and atashi women-leaning; anata and kimi can sound cold or bossy where a name would do.

chunks.label: He, she, that person
chunks.rationale: Lets you point to and talk about other people.
chunks.interference: kare and kanojo usually mean boyfriend and girlfriend, not just he and she.

chunks.label: Saying we
chunks.rationale: Lets you say we at different levels of casualness.
chunks.interference: oretachi is men's casual talk; watashitachi works for everyone.

chunks.label: Blunt you
chunks.rationale: Lets you recognise rough ways of saying you.
chunks.interference: omae is friendly among male friends but aggressive from strangers.

chunks.label: That guy, those guys
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk casually about people who aren't here.
chunks.interference: koitsu, soitsu and aitsu follow the same near, middle and far split as kore, sore and are.

chunks.label: We with -ra
chunks.rationale: Lets you make casual plurals and hear the we-words in songs.
chunks.interference: -ra sounds rougher than -tachi; bokura is softer than orera.

chunks.label: Formal and self words
chunks.rationale: Lets you mention someone respectfully, speak for a group, and say yourself.
chunks.interference: jibun jishin stresses the self; plain jibun is the everyday word.

drops.reason: Duplicate of 私たち (same word, written with kanji 達).
